name: Liquiritin

lead: Liquiritin is a flavonoid glycoside found in licorice root (Glycyrrhiza). In skincare it is used in brightening products aimed at uneven pigmentation, dark patches and dullness.
The appearance payoff is a more even, lighter-looking complexion. A small controlled trial of a liquiritin cream in women with melasma assessed pigment intensity and lesion size over weeks.

paras: It is applied topically as a cream or as an ingredient in licorice-extract serums, usually alongside sunscreen. The melasma trial used twice-daily application for 4 weeks, with participants told to avoid sun or use sunscreen.

Topical liquiritin has not been reported with major problems in the small trial, but safety data are limited. Separately, high oral intake of licorice's glycyrrhizinic acid is linked to hypertension and low potassium, and licorice extract should be avoided in pregnancy according to Wikipedia.

chain: Reported to affect melanin synthesis in treated skin
angle.text: Liquiritin is used in brightening creams to reduce the look of pigmented patches such as melasma.

lead: Liquiritin is the 4'-O-glucoside of the flavanone liquiritigenin, a compound from licorice with the formula C21H22O9 [1]. It is also isolated from Glycyrrhiza uralensis roots [1].

For appearance, it is one of several natural molecules reviewed as skin-whitening agents that affect melanin synthesis, alongside arbutin, glabridin, kojic acid and others [2]. A controlled clinical trial tested liquiritin cream on melasma [3].
Other published work on liquiritin is pharmacological, covering anti-inflammatory and other activities in lab models and reviews [4].

paras: In cosmetics, liquiritin appears in a list of natural depigmenting molecules reviewed in 2019 [2]. The licorice extracts it comes from are also used in brightening products.
Liquiritin is a flavanone glucoside of liquiritigenin, and is one of the flavonoids derived from licorice [1].

Licorice's glycyrrhizinic acid is linked to hypertension and low blood potassium at high intake, and licorice extract is to be avoided in pregnancy per Wikipedia [5]. These concerns concern glycyrrhizin-rich oral intake rather than topical liquiritin specifically.

In a controlled trial, 20 women with epidermal melasma applied liquiritin cream to one side of the face and a vehicle cream to the other twice daily for 4 weeks, with follow-up to 10 weeks and ratings of pigment intensity and lesion size [3].

timeline.event: Controlled trial of topical liquiritin cream for melasma published [3].
